response.sql:
WITH group_counts AS (
    SELECT 
        p.SEX,
        COUNT(*) as record_count
    FROM Laboratory l
    JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID
    WHERE p.SEX IS NOT NULL AND p.SEX != ''
    GROUP BY p.SEX
),
avg_count AS (
    SELECT AVG(record_count) as avg_val 
    FROM group_counts
),
above_avg_groups AS (
    SELECT 
        gc.SEX,
        gc.record_count
    FROM group_counts gc
    CROSS JOIN avg_count
    WHERE gc.record_count > avg_count.avg_val
),
total_count_above AS (
    SELECT SUM(record_count) as total 
    FROM above_avg_groups
)
SELECT 
    aag.SEX,
    aag.record_count,
    aag.record_count / tca.total as fraction,
    aag.record_count - ac.avg_val as above_average
FROM above_avg_groups aag
CROSS JOIN total_count_above tca
CROSS JOIN avg_count ac;

assumptions.assumption: "Empty string" for SEX is interpreted as both NULL and '' (empty string literal). These are typically treated equivalently in database contexts when excluding missing values.

"All these groups" in "as a fraction of the total over all these groups" refers to the set of groups displayed (those above average), not all groups. The total is the sum of record counts only for groups above the per-group average.

alternatives.interpretation: Filter only empty string literal ('') and not NULL values when excluding records
